verdict.rationale: Zoho Books gives an agent the access it needs to watch the ledger. Zoho MCP is documented for autonomous agents that "monitor, reason, and act", the REST API claims full parity with the web client, and banking/reconciliation endpoints are exposed. Built-in Zia AI claims to "spot anomalies before they become problems", but that is a one-line vendor tagline, and nothing describes how an agent would flag spend anomalies or duplicates, so the detection logic appears to be left to the user's agent. Missing for 10: documented duplicate-transaction detection, specifics of Zia's anomaly detection (what it flags, thresholds, alerts), an agent-facing anomaly or alert API or MCP tool, and independent or hands-on corroboration of pre-close anomaly flagging.
